summary: Mendon's rulings on the deck search and look (issue #368). Order Seppuku is governed by ONE predicate, MatchEngine.SeppukuTimingReason (src/L5R.Core/SeppukuTiming.cs): only in the Action phase, only for the player who holds priority (their own turn to act), and only with nothing pending (PendingChoice and every other decision-holding state; a guard test fails when a new Pending* field is unclassified). The command handler and QueryActions (the legal-action list the AI and the client read) both use it; as an action it now hands the opportunity to the other player. The Hesitation bar and the card-level rules are unchanged and checked beside it. A Terrain found by a search can no longer be discarded to its own 'discard a card' (excluded from the offered and accepted discards); with no other card in hand nothing is discarded, with no error (searchDiscardSkipped). Shared because it changes which actions QueryActions offers to every client and bot, plus the engine rules, tests and both decision docs.
validation: bash tools/check.sh --skip-client passed: 216 core, 59 published, 9 new seppuku-timing, 23 deck-search (new TerrainCannotBeDiscardedToItsOwnEffect), 15 deck-look, 27 AI (a Seppuku timing invariant runs at every decision of the full AI matches), 8 server, 7 transport, python content tests. Mutations caught: no Action-phase test, no turn-to-act test, PendingChoice dropped from the decision table, a stale-style block at ordinary opportunities, the found Terrain offered for its own discard, the command not refusing it, the empty-hand case still opening an unanswerable stage. Existing tests adapted only where the ruling demands: OrderSeppukuIsOpenAction, SeppukuBarred, InnateActionSeppukuIsBarred, SeppukuCannotInterruptASearch, FateTerrainToHandAndDiscard. Godot import/smoke left to CI.
remaining: None; ready for review. Note for Mendon: Seppuku now passes the opportunity to the other player after it resolves, like every other action (it used to leave priority where it was).
